scope: Controlled same-frame case15 f101 rightward angle ablation; manually tested 15 and 45 degrees around VLM-proposed 30 degrees. Not a search over all directions or angles.

15.visual: Stage2 is mild with little discernible parallax on plain background. Stage3 person/scene remain recognizable and face relatively clear, but by the middle one arm is poorly expressed and late both arms drop while the source keeps hands near the head; action fidelity failure.

30.visual: Stage2 orbit is somewhat more discernible, though blank background limits depth cue. Stage3 follows arm-to-head and leg progression better than the other two; late face/hands visibly blur. No full quality pass asserted.

45.visual: Stage2 gives the strongest visible side view; person remains framed but scene/mesh coverage falls. Stage3 retains a person but body/face appear to rotate progressively away and late hands/head/hoodie form drift from source action; more side-view impact trades off against motion/identity fidelity.

manual_relative_observation: Among these three tested rightward angles at f101, 30 degrees preserves the visible arm sequence most faithfully; 45 degrees shows a stronger side view but more pose/orientation drift; 15 degrees preserves face clarity but loses an arm action. This is a comparison of executed options, not proof of global best angle, final quality acceptance, or user preference.
metric_caveat: DWPose is a cross-view 2D proxy; person contrast proxy has a known false negative on historical case13 melt; mesh coverage is not a quality threshold. Final judgement uses actual native videos.

vlm_angle_feedback.method: Two Qwen3-VL-30B native-DD ballots with reversed candidate order, enlarged official-DWPose upper-body crops at middle/end frames, and all-frame 2D motion evidence; exact JSON and frame-reference validation passed.
vlm_angle_feedback.stable_choice: R30 among rightward 15/30/45 degrees at source f101
vlm_angle_feedback.limitations: The model still exaggerates R15/R45 body melting and understates the visible late blur of R30; in one ballot it also reverses a numeric comparison in prose. Treat the stable choice as a scoped recommendation, not trustworthy per-frame scoring, a global optimum, or final human quality acceptance.
